intent: The visual readout of its progress root's current value.
typical_uses: The percentage readout at the end of the row, beside a ProgressLabel

dont_use_when.situation: A number readout that is not a progress root's value

instead.target: text in the consuming application's own markup
instead.note: A ProgressValue renders only the nearest root's formatted value and is hidden from assistive technology; the kit ships no generic readout component.

invariants.text: The readout is always `aria-hidden`: the root's `aria-valuenow` carries the value to assistive technology, and the readout is for sighted users only.
With an indeterminate root the readout's span is empty - there is no percentage to show - and a function child receives the string "indeterminate" and a null value to decide what to show instead.

anti_patterns.dont: Pass text children to customize the readout
anti_patterns.do_instead: Pass a function child receiving the formatted value; a plain string child is ignored at runtime and rejected by tsc, so it never renders

a11y.by: the primitive's Progress.Value, which renders with aria-hidden always (verified in the @base-ui/react/progress source); progress.test.tsx asserts the rendered "42%" text

children.states: children is null, to render the root's formatted value, or a function of the formatted value and the raw value returning React nodes
children.because: `null | ((formattedValue: string | null, value: number | null) => ReactNode)` - a union of null and a callback. The compiler emits one JSON type per property, and a function has no JSON Schema representation.

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the value's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - neither expressible in JSON Schema.

style.states: style accepts a function of the value's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (status). A JSON Schema `object` would reject the function form, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through progress.module.css, not through this.

good.title: The live readout beside its caption

bad.title: Text children glued to the percentage
bad.why: children must be null or a function: a string is ignored at runtime and rejected by tsc, so the suffix never renders. A function child formats the readout instead.

children.description: TS: ((formattedValue: string | null, value: number | null) => ReactNode) | null | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. children is null, to render the root's formatted value, or a function of the formatted value and the raw value returning React nodes. `null | ((formattedValue: string | null, value: number | null) => ReactNode)` - a union of null and a callback. The compiler emits one JSON type per property, and a function has no JSON Schema representation.

render.description: TS: ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, ProgressValueState> | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies. Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the value's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - neither expressible in JSON Schema.

style.description: TS: CSSProperties | ((state: ProgressValueState) => CSSProperties | undefined) | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. style accepts a function of the value's state as well as a plain style object. Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (status). A JSON Schema `object` would reject the function form, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through progress.module.css, not through this.
